questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you control your vehicle better while turning.

questions.question: How can you stop a skid caused by pressing the gas pedal too hard?
questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal to stop a skid from over-acceleration. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: Can you use radial and bias-ply tires on the same vehicle?

options.text: Yes, but only on the rear axle.

questions.explanation: Do not use radial and bias-ply tires together on your vehicle.

questions.question: How do you parallel park correctly?

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Drive forward past the space, then back into it.
Drive forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space, then back into it. Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Get a full night's sleep before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a full night's sleep before your trip.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Get enough sleep the night before you drive. Other ways to prevent drowsiness include having someone ride with you, driving during times when you are normally awake, and avoiding medicines that cause drowsiness. Regular exercise also helps you stay alert.

questions.question: What should you check extra carefully before winter driving?
questions.explanation: Before driving in winter, make sure your coolant and antifreeze are at the correct levels.

questions.question: What should you do if you stop on the side of the road?
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Tell the carrier about problems that need fixing
Make sure the vehicle is inspected regularly
Hold people responsible for inspecting the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the carrier about problems that need fixing
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report informs the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: While passengers are on a bus, what are refueling in an enclosed space, towing the bus, and talking with passengers considered?
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must not talk with passengers, fuel the bus inside a building, or tow or push a disabled bus while passengers are on board. These are all prohibited practices.

questions.question: When driving a bus with passengers, what should a driver do?

options.text: Ask passengers to watch for hazards.

questions.explanation: A bus driver should not talk with passengers. This keeps the driver focused on the road.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your blood?
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Coffee and exercise cannot speed this up. Only time will remove alcohol from your blood.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Add more space between your vehicle and the one in front.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add more space between your vehicle and the one in front.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the space in front of your vehicle. This gives the tailgater room to pass safely. Speeding up does not help because the other driver may just tailgate faster.

questions.question: How should cargo on flatbed trailers be secured?
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down. This prevents it from shifting or falling during transport.

questions.question: How should you brake in a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the brakes several times before holding down the pedal.
Press the brake pedal as hard as possible every time you slow or stop.

questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in any other vehicle. ABS automatically prevents the wheels from locking up when you brake.

questions.question: When you change lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Other vehicles will get out of your way.
Wait to change lanes until you are in an intersection.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This helps you control your vehicle better and gives other drivers time to react to your movements.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, what should you check about emergency exits?

options.text: They are not accessible from inside the cab.

questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check that emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits must open easily, be in good condition, and close securely from the inside.

questions.question: What is the purpose of header boards?

options.text: Protect the driver in a crash

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver in a crash
questions.explanation: Header boards protect the driver from cargo that moves forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: If you are unsure how to put out a vehicle fire, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you do not know which fire extinguisher to use, especially for a hazardous materials fire, wait for firefighters to arrive and handle it.

questions.question: If you pull over to the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Let your taillights warn other drivers.
Keep your lights off to avoid distracting drivers.
Keep your door open to warn drivers.

questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Taillights alone are not enough because drivers may think you are moving normally and hit your vehicle.
